<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par138 />{{GHGheb|text=לְקָחַ֫נִי}}, while in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=2}} it is not resumed at all. This suppression of the retrospective pronoun<ref>The instances in which, instead of a retrospective pronoun, the main idea itself is repeated ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=32}}) are most probably all due to subsequent amplification of the original text by another hand.</ref> takes place especially when it (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=2}}) would represent an accusative of the object, or when it would be a separate pronoun representing a nominative of the subject in a noun-clause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=הַמַּ֫יִם אֲשֶׁר מִתַּחַת לָֽרָקִיעַ|translate=the waters, those, under the firmament}}, &c. In negative sentences, however, the retrospective pronoun is not infrequently added, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}; 7:2 {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=20|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה}}; but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר הוּא חַי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=3}}. The addition of {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} in a verbal clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=22|verse=13}}, is unusual.

The very frequent omission of the retrospective pronoun is noticeable in cases where the predicate of the qualifying clause is a {{GHGterm|verbum dicendi}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=10|verse=29}} ''we are journeying unto the place'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר אָמַר יְהוָֹה אֹתוֹ אֶתֵּן לָכֶם|translate=that}} place, ''the Lord said'' (of it), ''It will I give to you''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=40}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=17}}, 23, 24:5, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=43}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|c}}
2. When the substantive, followed by {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} and the qualifying clause, expresses an idea of ''place'', it may also be resumed by the adverbs of place {{GHGheb|text=שָׁם|translate=there}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫מָּה|translate=thither}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִשָּׁם|translate=thence}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=13|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=עַד־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר־הָיָה שָׁם אָֽהֳלֹה|translate=unto the place, that one, his tent had been there}}, i.e. ''where his tent had been''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=מִשָּׁם}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=21|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫מָּה}}. But even in this case the retrospective word may be omitted, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=64|verse=10}}, where {{GHGheb|text=שָׁם}} would be expected, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=2}}, where {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫מָּה}} would be expected.—When the appositional clause is added to a word of time, the retrospective pronoun is always omitted, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=31}} ''for all the days'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר בֶּן־יִשַׁי חַי}} ''those—the son of Jesse is living'' (''in them''); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=42}}; see Baumann, op. cit., p. 33.

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|d}}
3. If the governing substantive forms part of a statement made in the first or second person, the retrospective pronoun (or the subject of the appositional clause) is in the same person, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=4}} ''I am Joseph'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר־מְכַרְתֶּם אֹתִי}} ''he—ye sold me'', i.e. ''whom ye sold''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=23}}; 41:8 ''thou, Jacob'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר בְּחַרְתִּ֫יךָ}} ''he—I have chosen thee''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=16}} f.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=7}} ''I am the Lord'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר הֽוֹצֵאתִ֫יךָ}} ''he—I brought thee out'', &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=2}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=6}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|138|e}}
(2) Not depending (adjectivally) on a governing substantive, but itself expressing a substantival idea. Clauses introduced in this way may be called ''independent relative clauses''. This use of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is generally rendered in English by ''he who, he whom'', &c. (according to the context), or ''that which'', &c., or sometimes ''of such a kind as'' (''qualis''), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=14|verse=13}}<sup>''b''</sup>, and in a dependent relative clause {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=17}}. In reality, however, the {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is still a demonstrative belonging to the construction of the main clause as subject or object, or as a genitive dependent on a noun or preposition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר תָּאֹר יוּאָר}} ''iste—thou cursest'' (him)—''is cursed'', i.e. ''he whom thou cursest'', &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=22|verse=8}};<ref>The absolute use of {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} is very peculiar in the formula {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר הָיָה דְבַר יי׳ אֶל־|translate=this}} (is it)—''it came as the word of the Lord to''..., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=14|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=47|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=34|hidebook=1}}.</ref> {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} as object, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=1}},<section end=par138 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
